doc.title: Dave Valentin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Playing with Roland Hanna at the festival
summary: They traded common repertoire such as Autumn Leaves, Footprints and Oye Como Va, and Valentin plans to bring a Latin flavor to the event.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: No I don’t think so. I had to chuckle when I was listening to you and Roland Hanna this morning. It’s so interesting to hear musicians at these kind of events find a common ground.
You mentioned some tunes to him and he said now watch out, I’m twice your age. And he’d throw some back at you.
I told him watch out, I’m half your age.

Do you feel at all put on the spot when you get to these things to try to be able to — I’ve started this question badly — but I guess I almost envision myself in that position of trying to think of oh gosh, Roland Hanna, he probably knows a zillion things, now what’s in my repertoire that I can match with his. Is that a problem for you?

No. I think within that timeline there’s something that we know together. And then he just mentioned of course, which I forgot about, like “Autumn Leaves,” and “Carnival” and all those things. So just those two tunes alone could be an hour, depending on the stretch. And then he knew “Footprints,” and I showed him a little Montuno, like “Oye Como Va” type of thing.
Oh yeah? Well that will add a different flavor to these things.
Yeah. Because somebody told me it’s much of an older concept kind of thing.
Yeah. The people that come to these things have their tastes pretty much in the mainstream.
But I think they’ll welcome a little — see what happens.
Yeah, we’ll give them a little rice and beans and see what happens. Hope they don’t get gas.
